title: Inclusion of contracted fibre components in a common semistable model
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for each $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(C,D)$ have smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Let $f:(X,F)\to(C,D)$ be a stable $\eta$-modification and $g:(Y,G)\to(C,D)$ a semistable $\eta$-modification. Suppose $(W,E)$ is semistable and $a:(W,E)\to(X,F)$ and $b:(W,E)\to(Y,G)$ are $\eta$-modifications with $fa=gb$. For every $s\in S$ and every irreducible component $Z$ of $W_s$, if $b_s(Z)$ is a point then $a_s(Z)$ is a point. This asserts only an inclusion of the sets of contracted fibre components; it does not assume or conclude a morphism $Y\to X$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.
